segments.text: One signature can hand a stranger your entire wallet. And the pop-up asking for it is written in code, not English.
Here's a common trap: an unlimited approval, to a contract nobody has verified, created just four days ago.
One click, and you get it in plain English.
Risky. Whoever controls that contract could move all of your USDC, at any time, until you revoke it.
Compare that with a limited approval to Uniswap, that expires in thirty minutes.
Likely safe. Same kind of pop-up, a very different risk.
For your own wallet, paste your address, pick a chain, and PlainText checks every approval you've ever given.
A full check costs ten cents in USDC, paid per check. No account, no subscription, and nothing is stored.
AI agents can use it too: they pay per call with x402, on Base or Solana.
